title: Entries between San Francisco housing funds grew above $20 million before reconciliation

beats.text: San Francisco housing accounts could balance overall while individual funds did not.
The accounting system recorded the difference as money owed between programs.

visual.kicker: The project ledgers could balance overall while individual funds did not

beats.text: A 2014 cleanup used project cash and a federally approved loan.
By 2017 the balances were above $17 million.

visual.kicker: The balances exceeded $17 million and then $20 million

beats.text: The next year they exceeded $20 million.
Those were successive balances, not cash leaving the Authority.

visual.kicker: The balances exceeded $17 million and then $20 million

beats.text: The Authority manually removed entries that did not represent actual obligations.

visual.kicker: Manual review reduced the balance, but more than $5 million remained

beats.text: More than $5 million remained at the end of 2019.

visual.kicker: Manual review reduced the balance, but more than $5 million remained

beats.text: The 2020 audit recorded the corrective action as implemented.

visual.kicker: The FY2020 audit separated corrective action from ordinary interprogram balances

beats.text: It also reported $2,656,010 in normal interprogram balances.
Those balances cancel out in the consolidated financial statements.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
